candidate.title: 3P-Seq
candidate.scope: The 3P-Seq (poly(A)-position profiling by sequencing) row of the assigned Illumina poster, with its depicted splint-mediated tagging, affinity selection, reverse transcription, RNase H processing and cDNA endpoint. The independent cP-RNA-Seq and 2P-seq rows and clipped surrounding chemistry are context, not target alternatives. The graph retains the poster’s T1-before-ligation route; primary-supported interpretation distinguishes the tail-only RT and released RNA from the later cDNA library. This is schematic architecture, not an executable Jan et al. protocol.

operations.label: T1 RNase partial digest
operations.description: Partially cleave the RNA body, producing shortened RNA fragments while retaining a poly(A)-ending fragment. The graph keeps the poster’s pre-ligation placement. Jan et al. report this digestion after adaptor ligation; this local input history therefore describes the schematic, not the literal order of that primary protocol.
operations.mechanism: T1 nuclease cleavage after G residues is reported by Jan et al.; the poster depicts interrupted RNA after partial digestion.
operations.information_effect: Reduces upstream transcript length while retaining the transcript-to-poly(A)-end association on the surviving 3′ fragment.

operations.label: Ligate biotinylated primer
operations.description: Use the depicted biotinylated adaptor/splint assembly to append a capture and primer-binding handle at the poly(A) tail end of the RNA fragment. The caption Biotinylated splint primer identifies the reagent assembly rather than an independent alternative workflow.
operations.mechanism: Splint-mediated ligation joins the RNA 3′ end to the 5′-phosphorylated biotinylated adaptor; the DNA splint bridges the junction and is not the retained covalent biotin tag.
operations.information_effect: Associates the transcript end with an affinity tag and an adaptor-directed priming site. End-favoring ligation supports terminal enrichment; it does not establish perfect specificity for every captured molecule.

operations.description: Select the biotin-bearing RNA 3′ fragments through streptavidin affinity and retain them for primer extension. The primary implementation binds these molecules to streptavidin-coated beads; no pooling or new branch is shown.

operations.label: Anneal primer and reverse-transcribe
operations.description: Anneal a primer to the appended adaptor site and extend it on the captured RNA. Although the poster draws a long duplex, Jan et al. restrict this step to the poly(A) tail with dTTP alone; the output here uses that primary-supported interpretation.
operations.mechanism: Adaptor-directed reverse transcription with dTTP as the only deoxynucleoside triphosphate generates a poly(dT) complement to the poly(A) tract.
operations.information_effect: Creates the RNA/DNA tail hybrid needed for RNase H processing. It does not yet convert the upstream transcript-end sequence into the final sequencing cDNA.

operations.label: RNase H digestion
operations.description: Process the RNA/DNA tail hybrid and release transcript-end RNA from the captured complex. operations.mechanism: RNase H treatment of the tail hybrid releases RNA fragments; incomplete digestion near the duplex terminus leaves residual adenylates.
operations.information_effect: Separates the transcript-end RNA from the capture assembly while preserving residual non-genomic A residues as evidence of its polyadenylated origin.

method_scopes.rationale: All five captioned transformations in the 3P-Seq row apply to this target. Biotinylated splint primer is a reagent/component of ligation. o_library is an explicitly paper-supported, broad endpoint interface, not a sixth arrow in the poster. The row is identified by the card title and independently matched collection heading/caption. Jan et al. describe the named method, but their ligation precedes T1 digestion; the drawing reverses those two operations. That difference is retained in the local input history and is not asserted to be a validated interchangeable order. Corrections c_tail_rt and c_rna_release resolve the consequential RT/product-identity discrepancies. Adjacent 2P-seq remains a separate assay even though Spies et al. discuss both.
